sentences.text: Through this part, higher capital gains lower a typical person's predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) slowly at first, then faster: from about 63% at 0 to about 9% at 6849 US dollars, flattening out near the bottom because the predicted chance cannot go much lower.

For people whose highest education is 9th grade the fall is smaller, again slowly at first, then faster, from about 44% to about 6%, and for people born in Jamaica it ends higher, from about 71% to about 16%.
It is made of two parts: the main capital-gains curve, and a second one that adds nothing until about 4883 US dollars, then lowers the chance steadily (about 63% to about 56% through it alone).

This part adds up most characteristics, each on its own: a higher education level lowers a typical person's predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) steadily, from about 84% at 7 to about 35% at 13 on the 1-16 scale, and higher capital losses lower it steadily, from about 63% at 0 to about 31% at 1887 US dollars.

Being married to a member of the armed forces lowers it to below 1%, while a marital status other than married, divorced or widowed raises it to about 97%, being divorced to about 95% and widowed to about 91%; being a wife lowers it to about 41% and being a woman raises it to about 74%.

reference_patient.definition: the typical patient: the median training patient for every number and the most common training category for every category (not a real patient)

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients
